title: Multiple phases in K2Cr3As3: a playground for manipulating topological superconductivity
authors: Seigo Ogawa, Tomoki Miyoshi, Saki Uchida, Kazuaki Matano, Shinji Kawasaki, Yoshihiko Inada, Guo-qing Zheng
abstract: Spin-triplet topological superconductors are rare but of fundamental interest as they can host Majorana bound states that can be used in fault-tolerant quantum computing. Recent efforts have been devoted to searching for spin-triplet states in U-based compounds, but these materials have a low transition temperature (Tc) and coexisting competing orders, which creates significant experimental challenges and often leads to contradictory conclusions. The Cr-based candidate K2Cr3As3 offers a promising alternative: it has a much higher Tc of 6.2 K and no magnetic order. Here we report a hallmark signature of spin-triplet superconductivity arising from the internal spin degrees of freedom via nuclear magnetic resonance measurements, and demonstrate the high tunability of the topological phases. We discovered three distinct superconducting phases and revealed the evolution of the paired-spins direction (d(k)-vector). At low magnetic fields, K2Cr3As3 evolves from a helical (Phase A) to a chiral state (Phase B) with a rotation of the d(k)-vector from in-plane to out-of-plane direction upon cooling, although both phases have point nodes in the gap. A linenodal gap is realized in the high-field Phase C, where the d(k)-vector lies in the basal plane. These findings establish K2Cr3As3 as a model spin-triplet superconductor and a promising platform for manipulating topological phases.
summary: This work establishes K2Cr3As3 as a model spin-triplet superconductor by experimentally revealing three distinct superconducting phases (A, B, C). Using NMR measurements, the authors map out how the pairing symmetry and the direction of the d(k)-vector evolve under applied magnetic fields. These findings highlight the material's potential for manipulating topological quantum states.
main_problem: Investigating spin-triplet superconductivity, a state crucial for hosting Majorana bound states in quantum computing.
main_result: The authors identified three distinct superconducting phases (A, B, and C) in K2Cr3As3, demonstrating the high tunability of its topological superconducting phases by manipulating magnetic fields.
method: Measurements utilized Nuclear Magnetic Resonance ($	ext{}^{75}	ext{As}$-NMR) to probe the spin susceptibility and gap structure, alongside $ac$ susceptibility measurements.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Cr-based compound K2Cr3As3, which is proposed as a non-magnetic alternative to U-based superconductors. The analysis maps out the superconducting phase diagram using magnetic field (B) and temperature (T).
key_observables: Knight shift ($K$), spin-lattice relaxation rate ($1/T_1$), and the evolution of the pairing vector $\mathbf{d}(\mathbf{k})$.
important_parameters: Critical temperature ($T_c \ge 6.2 	ext{ K}$), applied magnetic field (up to $13 	ext{ T}$), and temperature dependence exponents ($\propto T^{-3}$ vs. $\propto T^{-5}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on interpreting the temperature power laws of $1/T_1$ to distinguish between line-nodal and point-nodal gap structures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing multiple superconducting phases (A, B, C) as a function of magnetic field for $B\parallel c$, detailing characteristic temperatures ($T^*$) derived from NMR measurements.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes experimental signatures—NMR Knight shift and $1/T_1$ dependence—to map out the phase diagram, identifying distinct superconducting states characterized by different $\mathbf{d}(\mathbf{k})$-vector orientations and gap symmetries.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the detailed mapping of topological phases and symmetry breaking in response to external fields provides a rich platform for studying emergent quantum order parameters relevant to advanced condensed matter physics.
